## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Hetuduka* (Patthana 8.1) is a text of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and concluding treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The title designates the "root dyad" (*hetuduka*), a foundational Abhidhamma classification that divides all phenomena into those that are root causes (*hetū dhammā*) and those that are not root causes (*na hetū dhammā*) [U Kyaw Khine 1999]. In the conditional methodology of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the text examines how phenomena arise in dependence on roots or non-roots according to conditional relations (such as root condition, *hetupaccaya*), including negative analytical treatments (*hetuduke na-hetuduka*) [Nyanatiloka 2007].
DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse for this text, recording 647 matching passages shared with 65 other texts across the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial overlaps occur with other analytical and permuted treatments of the root dyad in the *Paṭṭhāna*, such as *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1; 87 matches), *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1; 116 matches), *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1; 88 matches), and *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1; 25 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
